notes: G-1 IMP-0018: file-based argument marshalling for payloads near the Windows CreateProcess 32,767-character cap. Live named probes exit 0. Did not run global unit_manifest.py --write. cloud ok=true is not delivery. Restrictive temp-file permissions are 0600 inside a 0700 directory; files are deleted on every exit path.
question_or_target: Implement a marshalling layer that writes any argument payload above a conservative threshold to a temp file and passes the PATH, because Windows CreateProcess caps the command line at 32,767 characters and an over-limit invocation dies with OS error 206 before any code runs.

residual_unknowns.claim: Exact CreateProcess fail length was not re-measured on a Windows box in this Linux worktree. The guard uses the documented 32,767 cap. Linux SC_ARG_MAX =2097152 would accept a 40,000-character argv, so the inline OS error 206 here is the Windows-compat spawn guard, not this kernel's ARG_MAX.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: On a Windows host, spawn the same 40,000-character argv through CreateProcessW without the guard and confirm WinError 206; then confirm the file transport still round-trips.

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 independently confirms OS error 206 on the inline path, restrictive 0600/0700 temp permissions, and deletion on the injected-failure path. A check that only asserted the marshalled success path would miss a leak or a fake inline fail.

title: File-based argument marshalling for payloads near the command-line limit
